name: Tu Hsun-ho
bio: Tu Hsun-ho was a late T’ang poet who took his degree in AD 891 and died about AD 904, according to the chronology of poets in The Jade Mountain.
The poem here is Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu’s version in The Jade Mountain (1929), given with the poet’s name as spelled here.

poems.title: A Sigh in the Spring Palace
poems.author: Tu Hsun-ho
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Knowing beauty my misfortune,
I face my mirror with a sigh.
To please a fastidious emperor,
How shall I array myself? . . .
Birds flock and sing when the wind is warm,
Flower-shadows climb when the sun is high —
And year after year girls in the south
Are picking hibiscus, dreaming of love!
